steps.what: Read relevant patient history, current medicines and existing supplement use
Look up the applicable approved vitamin and mineral guidance
Discuss diet, current supplement use and patient concerns
Recommend appropriate vitamin or mineral use and explain the individual advice
First enter and verify the actual recommendation and relevant new facts
Save the author's supplement advice entry

tasks.design: Configure source and topic filters for the existing approved guidance in {DOCS}. The midwife interprets the guidance, asks about actual use, gives the individual recommendation and first records it in the {OTHER} clinical-record system; no recommendation or dose is generated automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the relevant guidance can involve repeated navigation, while the recommendation depends on individual facts.
tasks.enabler_now: Native guidance filters can reduce search without interpreting the patient's clinical situation.
tasks.still_hard: Diet, existing medicines, supplement use and patient concerns need personal assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The midwife explains an appropriate recommendation and checks what the patient is already taking.
tasks.altitude: A little less guidance navigation; clinical authority and advice remain unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss dietary intake and supplement use
reach.learn: Clear intake questions and distinguishing general guidance from individual advice

evidence.claim: Source and topic filters can reduce navigation within approved guidance; this is model knowledge, not evidence for automated supplement advice.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual advice and its clinical entry used for continuity of care. It does not invent a patient message, prescription transaction or separate supplement register.

The practice's clinical owner supplies approved guidance with topic, version and review date. Existing clinical records supply known history; the patient clarifies current diet and use in s3. The midwife first enters the recommendation and new relevant facts in s5, with all twenty-four entry hours retained.
Test native guidance search and filters first. Two of ten lookup hours are navigation; eight hours of reading and checking applicability remain. No clean structured dietary feed is assumed.
The one-hour ordinary same-system author save stays fully retained and has no self-approval gate. No new clinical decision tool or ambient recording is introduced.
unknowns: Whether approved guidance already has effective filters
How often current supplement use is missing from the record
research_questions: Can a native topic filter remove navigation without suggesting a patient-specific recommendation?

already_counted.description: Read applicable guidance and first record the actual advice

incremental.description: Check guidance filter links and version metadata

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: two guidance-navigation hours removed less 0.3 upkeep gives 1.7. Cautious case: the practice already bookmarks the relevant guidance, retaining all ten lookup hours and adding no extra filter or upkeep. Clinical reading, discussion, recommendation, first entry and author saving remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide community health and social resource information

steps.what: Ask about the patient's practical health and social support needs
Look up local community health and social resource details
Confirm uncertain service availability or access conditions with the provider
Explain relevant resources and answer the patient's practical access questions
Prepare the actual contact information sheet for the selected resources
Check final contact details and intended patient recipient
Hand the checked resource contact sheet to the patient or caregiver

tasks.design: Configure native locality and service-type filters in the existing {DOCS} resource directory and reuse selected fields in the actual contact sheet. The midwife confirms uncertain access conditions, explains options and checks the final sheet before giving it to the patient.
tasks.previous_blocker: Resource details are dispersed and access conditions can be stale.
tasks.enabler_now: Directory filters and contact-sheet templates can remove repeated navigation and layout.
tasks.still_hard: Availability, eligibility and practical suitability often need direct confirmation.
tasks.human_edge: The midwife understands barriers and helps the patient choose a realistic next contact.
tasks.altitude: Less resource navigation and handout layout; personal explanation remains.

reach.task: Help patients locate suitable support services
reach.learn: Local access conditions and checking resource freshness

evidence.claim: A maintained resource directory can be filtered by locality and service type and reused in a contact sheet; this is model knowledge, not a measured referral outcome.

assumptions: Boundary is information provision, not making a referral or transmitting patient data to a provider. The sheet is actual contact information used by the patient, not a new trailing encounter log.

The practice's existing directory owner supplies provider, locality, service type, contact, access conditions and last-check date. Missing or stale details are manually confirmed in s3 and first written into the actual selected sheet in s5. If no maintained directory exists, lookup remains manual.

Test native filters and templates first. Ten of twenty-five lookup hours are repeated search navigation; fifteen remain for suitability and source reading. Two of eight sheet hours are repeated layout; six remain for entering and checking actual details. Ordinary author saves are included and ungated.

The final sheet and recipient exist before s6. The gate applies only to actual physical delivery in s7; changed details require another check. No directory-maintenance task is silently transferred to another role.
unknowns: Whether the resource directory is actually maintained
How often availability must be checked by phone
Whether contact sheets already use templates
research_questions: Can current directory fields support locality lookup without creating new data collection work?

already_counted.description: Read resource details, first write the contact sheet and check final meaning

incremental.description: Maintain filters and template mappings and investigate stale displayed details

approvals.approved_version: Exact resource contact sheet and patient or caregiver recipient checked in s6; changes require a fresh check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: ten lookup-navigation and two layout hours removed, less one upkeep hour, gives 11. Cautious case: locally relevant providers lack directory metadata and all twenty-five search hours remain; the actual contact-sheet layout still removes two hours, less one upkeep, giving 1. Provider confirmation and patient conversation remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile and evaluate clinical practice statistics

steps.what: Define the practice cohort, reporting period and statistics to compare
Copy existing practice and registry statistical tables into the comparison workbook
Reconcile cohort totals, missing fields and statistical definitions
Compile the practice statistics into comparable tables and charts
Evaluate practice statistics and write limitations and implications for care
Save the author's evaluated practice statistics

tasks.design: Use native exports or existing comparison views from the {OTHER} maternity-record and clinical-registry systems before building a custom dashboard. Link the existing tables to a {SPREADSHEET} comparison template, automate fixed reconciliation checks and repeated chart setup, and retain the midwife's cohort and clinical interpretation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing statistical tables can be copied and reformatted for a local practice comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: Registry feedback and native exports can supply existing figures without re-keying them.
tasks.still_hard: Case mix, missing observations and differing denominators can make comparisons misleading.
tasks.human_edge: The midwife interprets whether a difference suggests a care issue or an incomparable population.

ambition.what: Review a specific practice outcome after a comparable new registry period becomes available

tasks.altitude: Less table copying and formatting; evaluation of clinical implications stays with the midwife.

reach.role: health information technologist and medical registrar
reach.task: Reconcile clinical dataset definitions for quality review
reach.learn: Cohort provenance, missingness and comparison limits

evidence.claim: Perined returns practice figures for comparison through mijnPerined; this supports reuse of existing statistical feedback, not a measured time saving.

assumptions: Boundary is a local practice statistical review, not first recording of clinical encounters or transmitting a new national dataset. Existing clinical capture and registry calculation runtime earn no saving here.

Care clinicians already create the source episode records as part of actual care. Existing registry and practice tables supply reporting period, cohort definition, denominator, outcome count, missing count and measure version. The midwife defines the review cohort in s1 and manually investigates absent or incompatible metadata within retained s3 and s5 time.

Test existing registry comparison views first; if they already remove manual copying and chart work, there is no such baseline to save. The central branch is an observed manual local comparison using existing tables, to be validated before adoption.

S2 removes twenty hours of second entry of already calculated tables, not statistical runtime. Seven of twenty reconciliation hours are fixed count and completeness comparisons; thirteen remain for definition repair. Nine of fifteen chart hours are repeated layout and series placement; six remain for checking labels and denominators.
All twenty-nine interpretation hours remain. The one-hour author save is fully retained, internal and ungated. No extra report send or clinical decision automation is added.
unknowns: Whether native registry views already meet the local review need
Availability of export metadata and denominator definitions
research_questions: Can each exported value retain its cohort, denominator, period and definition version through the local comparison?

already_counted.description: Repair definition mismatches, check comparisons and evaluate clinical implications

incremental.description: Maintain measure mappings and verify new registry periods and chart labels

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: twenty table-copy hours, seven fixed-reconciliation hours and nine chart-layout hours removed, less three upkeep hours, gives 33. Cautious case: a portal lacks a usable export, retaining all twenty table-copy hours; fixed count checks and repeat chart layout still remove sixteen hours, less three upkeep, giving 13. Interpretation and definition repair retain their time. If native feedback already performs the whole workflow, this additional tool is unnecessary and no saving should be claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify the birth record and identity evidence required for the certificate
First record certificate facts missing from the existing birth documentation
Copy verified identity and birth fields into the birth certificate form
Complete individual certificate fields and correct unsupported form mappings
Check the exact final certificate against identity and birth evidence
Certify the checked birth certificate in the authorised local process

tasks.design: Configure the applicable certificate template in {DOCS} to reuse verified fields from the {OTHER} maternity-record system. Retain missing-fact capture, individual form completion and full identity and birth-evidence checks; official certification remains a separate human action after the final certificate exists.
tasks.previous_blocker: Certificate forms repeat verified birth data but local forms and authority differ.
tasks.enabler_now: Native field mappings can populate an exact form without generating facts or certifying it.
tasks.still_hard: Names, identity evidence, corrections and local certification authority need personal verification.
tasks.human_edge: The authorised midwife attests to verified facts and resolves inconsistencies.
tasks.altitude: Less re-keying into the certificate; authority and responsibility for certification remain unchanged.

reach.task: Check identity and source evidence for official health documentation
reach.learn: Exact field provenance and local certification requirements

evidence.claim: Verified record fields can populate a fixed document template; this is model knowledge and does not establish a midwife's certification authority in any country.

assumptions: This branch applies only where the midwife actually completes and certifies the relevant birth document. Local rules determine the document and authorised signer; no claim is made that the midwife issues the civil registry's certificate everywhere.

The birth record supplies birth date, time, place and relevant birth identifiers; identity evidence supplies required names and identifiers. The midwife verifies these in s1 and first records missing facts in s2. Obtaining or clarifying missing evidence stays within those retained forty hours.

Test native record-to-form mapping first. S3 removes thirty hours of re-keying verified facts into a distinct certificate form. No first clinical capture or ordinary same-system save is removed; normal saves remain inside form completion.

All fifteen correction hours and fourteen final-check hours remain, including unsupported mappings. Certification is a real attestation, not an author save. The final form exists before s5; changes invalidate the check. Any later filing or send would need its own observed step and is not invented here.
unknowns: Availability of a compatible certificate form
research_questions: Can the native form mapping preserve exact source names and birth fields without implying unsupported certification authority?

already_counted.description: Complete individual fields, repair unsupported mappings and verify the exact final certificate

incremental.description: Check certificate template and field mappings after local form changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed certificate checked against source evidence in s5 within the authorised local process; changes require a fresh check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: thirty certificate re-entry hours removed less one mapping-upkeep hour gives 29. Cautious case: a changed local form retains twenty-five of the thirty re-entry hours, with only five supported identity fields still reused; less one upkeep hour gives 4. First fact capture, corrections, final verification and certification remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Clinical advice and personal support remain central. Existing registry feedback, resource views and document mappings can remove specific copying and layout actions.
reach: Patient representative: improve practical resource access guidance
Medical records specialist: strengthen source and identity checks
skills_to_grow: Clinical cohort comparability and denominator interpretation
Exact birth-document field mapping and local authority checks
role.ambitious_version: A midwife who can review practice patterns and provide clearer practical information with less repeated entry, while keeping advice and certification personally accountable.
